task.description: Run the full suite (owed since ISSUE-FIXER's own attempt was killed by an external 580s timeout wrapper, not a test failure) after SECURITY-REVIEWER PASS and REVIEWER PASS on the oidcc 3.8.0->3.9.0 / bandit 1.12.4->1.12.5 lockfile-only bump. Report real pass/fail counts and diagnose any failure as pre-existing/known vs. a genuine regression caused by the dependency bump.

result.summary:
Started letflow-1's own postgres/keycloak containers (`docker compose up -d`, required sudo in this shell due to docker-group permission -- both were already Up/healthy: letflow-1-postgres-1 on 0.0.0.0:5463->5432 matching this checkout's untracked .env LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5463, letflow-1-keycloak-1 healthy). Ran `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh && TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 scripts/test_parallel.sh` in the foreground as a single blocking call (no backgrounding, no Monitor, no cross-turn wait -- per explicit instruction given this exact run already stalled twice on this failure mode) and let it run to completion.

Exact output:
```
test_parallel: N=4 (source: env override)
test_parallel: pre-compiling MIX_ENV=test (single compile, before any partition launches)
test_parallel: TEST_POOL_SIZE=21 (computed: N=4, max_connections=100, superuser_reserved=3, headroom=10, nonpool_reserve=2)
test_parallel: seeding 4 per-partition build paths from _build/test (sequential)
test_parallel: partition logs in /tmp/letflow_test_parallel.Y2hEvy
test_parallel: TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP=tp3364619 (shared by all 4 partitions)
partition 1: 735 tests, 2 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
partition 2: 801 tests, 4 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
partition 3: 736 tests, 0 properties, 2 failures, exit 2
partition 4: 779 tests, 0 properties, 0 failures, exit 0
---
combined: 3051 tests, 6 properties, 2 failures (3055/3057 passed)
```

Combined total across all 4 partitions: 3055 passed / 3057 run, 2 failures. Diagnosed the 2 failures by reading partition 3's log directly (`/tmp/letflow_test_parallel.Y2hEvy/partition-3.log`, its own `Result: 734/736 passed, 1 excluded` / `Failed: 2 tests` lines at the end): both are in `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest` ('rust pin (REQ-165) a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row...' at test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs:289, and '...a matching rust pin reports OK with no mismatch' at :274), both failing identically with `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)` at lib/system.ex:1141 -- i.e. this host's environment has no `rustc` binary on PATH, so any test that shells out to `rustc --version` errors before it can assert anything. This is the exact pre-existing/known failure class flagged in this task's briefing (rustc-ENOENT in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest) -- an environment gap unrelated to Elixir/Erlang or any application dependency, and specifically unrelated to oidcc/bandit: neither package is invoked anywhere in this test file or its stacktrace. No auth/HTTP-path test, no oidcc test, no bandit/HTTP-adapter test, and no test outside CheckToolchainTest failed. Confirmed this is not a new regression: the failure is a missing OS-level tool on this dev host, not a code or dependency-version defect, and would fail identically on the pre-bump commit. No :wasm_hang flake and no Lua wall-clock timeout (ISS-0426) were observed in this run.

Conclusion: full suite is green modulo the one known, pre-existing, environment-only rustc-toolchain gap. No regression traceable to the oidcc 3.9.0 / bandit 1.12.5 bump. Recommend ORCH proceed to merge; the CheckToolchainTest failures are a standing environment issue (rustc not installed on this host) tracked separately from ISS-0420 and not a merge blocker for this lockfile-only security fix.

issues.description: Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest's 'rust pin (REQ-165)' tests (test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs:274 and :289) fail with Erlang :enoent because `rustc` is not installed on this host's PATH. Pre-existing, environment-only, unrelated to ISS-0420's oidcc/bandit bump. Not fixed here since it is out of this task's scope (dependency-version security fix only) and does not affect this branch's mergeability.
